I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Women and children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights, so that victims need to have their dignity protected and their right to live guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence against women and children is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for women and children physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

The existence of women and child victims of violence has not yet received adequate services, therefore comprehensive implementation of Protection for Women and Children is required.

In 2014 the Regional Government and DPRD established Regional Regulation Number 12 concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children. However, the said PERDA requires amendments related to institutional matters to be aligned with the latest regulations at the National level. In addition, the PERDA has also not comprehensively regulated matters related to protection implementation efforts that guarantee the fulfillment of victims' rights to truth, justice, recovery and guarantees of non-recurrence of cases, therefore a new regional regulation is needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This new Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for Women and Children particularly in terms of institutional matters, forms and mechanisms of prevention, prevention of acts of violence, accompaniment mechanisms, services for victims of acts of violence and empowerment of victims of acts of violence.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF CENTRAL MALUKU
NUMBER 5 OF 2022
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND
CHILD VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Women and children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights, so that victims need to have their dignity protected and their right to live guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence against women and children is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for women and children physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

The existence of women and child victims of violence has not yet received adequate services, therefore comprehensive implementation of Protection for Women and Children is required.

In 2014 the Regional Government and DPRD established Regional Regulation Number 12 concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children. However, the said PERDA requires amendments related to institutional matters to be aligned with the latest regulations at the National level. In addition, the PERDA has also not comprehensively regulated matters related to protection implementation efforts that guarantee the fulfillment of victims' rights to truth, justice, recovery and guarantees of non-recurrence of cases, therefore a new regional regulation is needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This new Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for Women and Children particularly in terms of institutional matters, forms and mechanisms of prevention, prevention of acts of violence, accompaniment mechanisms, services for victims of acts of violence and empowerment of victims of acts of violence.

Paragraph 1 Point a What is meant by "Early rescue of victims from acts of violence" is that victims have the right to rescue action at the time violence occurs if the victim's safety is threatened. This rescue action must be carried out by village/sub-district officials at the victim's place of residence or at the location where the violence occurred. Village/sub-district officials must immediately coordinate with the nearest security officers.
Point b What is meant by "Emergency medical treatment for victims" is when the victim suffers sufficiently severe injuries, then village/sub-district officials or medical personnel or security officers or family/community members who are aware of the occurrence of the act of violence must bring the victim to the nearest service facility to provide emergency assistance before the victim is taken to the hospital for further treatment.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF CENTRAL MALUKU
NUMBER 5 OF 2022
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND
CHILD VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Women and children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights, so that victims need to have their dignity protected and their right to live guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence against women and children is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for women and children physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

The existence of women and child victims of violence has not yet received adequate services, therefore comprehensive implementation of Protection for Women and Children is required.

In 2014 the Regional Government and DPRD established Regional Regulation Number 12 concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children. However, the said PERDA requires amendments related to institutional matters to be aligned with the latest regulations at the National level. In addition, the PERDA has also not comprehensively regulated matters related to protection implementation efforts that guarantee the fulfillment of victims' rights to truth, justice, recovery and guarantees of non-recurrence of cases, therefore a new regional regulation is needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This new Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for Women and Children particularly in terms of institutional matters, forms and mechanisms of prevention, prevention of acts of violence, accompaniment mechanisms, services for victims of acts of violence and empowerment of victims of acts of violence.

CHAPTER V
COMPLAINT AND HANDLING PROCEDURES
Article 25
(1) Complaints of violence victims to P2TP2A may be submitted by the victim, family, community members, police officers, volunteer assistants, or social workers.
(2) The head or officers present at P2TP2A are obligated to serve victims based on the provisions as referred to in Article 21.
(3) The head or officers of P2TP2A shall immediately handle victims in accordance with established procedures.
(4) The head or officers of P2TP2A, within a maximum period of 24 (twenty-four) hours from receiving the victim's complaint, are obligated to report it to the nearest police officer.

Article 30
(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector in the implementation of protection for women and children.
(2) The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1), is carried out through:
a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for women and children victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence; and
d. fostering and increasing economic independence of women victims of violence.
(3) The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) is implemented in the form of a joint agreement.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF CENTRAL MALUKU
NUMBER 5 OF 2022
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND
CHILD VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Women and children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights, so that victims need to have their dignity protected and their right to live guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence against women and children is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for women and children physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

The existence of women and child victims of violence has not yet received adequate services, therefore comprehensive implementation of Protection for Women and Children is required.

In 2014 the Regional Government and DPRD established Regional Regulation Number 12 concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children. However, the said PERDA requires amendments related to institutional matters to be aligned with the latest regulations at the National level. In addition, the PERDA has also not comprehensively regulated matters related to protection implementation efforts that guarantee the fulfillment of victims' rights to truth, justice, recovery and guarantees of non-recurrence of cases, therefore a new regional regulation is needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This new Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for Women and Children particularly in terms of institutional matters, forms and mechanisms of prevention, prevention of acts of violence, accompaniment mechanisms, services for victims of acts of violence and empowerment of victims of acts of violence.

a. to carry out efforts to prevent violence against women and children;
b. to carry out handling efforts for women and children victims of violence; and
c. to carry out rehabilitation efforts including recovery, empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence.
(3) The functions of P2TP2A are:
a. as a data and information center regarding women and children;
b. as a service center for women and children victims of violence; and
c. as an empowerment center for women and children.

Article 23
(1) In addition to services for victims as referred to in Article 20, Article 21, and Article 22, the Regional Government is obligated to provide assistance services for victims.
(2) Assistance services for victims may be implemented in cooperation with persons or institutions providing services for victims.
(3) The assistance mechanism as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be implemented in accordance with standard operating procedures established by a Regent Regulation.

Article 5
Letter a: Sufficiently clear.
Letter b: What is meant by special handling is handling for women and children victims of violence who require guaranteed security protection. Special handling is carried out through Safe House services and in cooperation with the police and the Witness and Victim Protection Agency (LPSK).
Letter c: What is meant by physical health services is in the form of: visum and treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims, carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
What is meant by mental health services is examination and treatment aimed at restoring the psyche/soul of victims as a result of acts of violence experienced, carried out by clinical psychologists and/or psychiatrists. Letter d: Sufficiently clear.
Letter e: Sufficiently clear.

(1) In handling victims, P2TP2A is obligated to establish networks with government or private hospitals for treatment and health recovery.

Article 11
(1) To coordinate the duties and responsibilities as referred to in Article 7, the Regional Government shall establish an Integrated Service Unit.
(2) The Integrated Service Unit as referred to in paragraph (1) is P2TP2A.

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 32
(1) The community participates in the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.

a. establishing protection units or complaint posts for women and children victims of violence within community organizations and/or within the Negeri community, Administrative Negeri/kelurahan
b. independently conducting socialization of the rights of women and children;

Article 6
In the event of an act of violence, every victim has the right to receive assistance both psychologically and legally as well as to obtain guarantees for their rights related to their status as a wife, mother, child, family member or as a member of society.

Fourth Part
Empowerment of Victims of Violence

Part Two
Partnership

Article 21
Paragraph 1 Point a What is meant by "Early rescue of victims from acts of violence" is that victims have the right to rescue action at the time violence occurs if the victim's safety is threatened. This rescue action must be carried out by village/sub-district officials at the victim's place of residence or at the location where the violence occurred. Village/sub-district officials must immediately coordinate with the nearest security officers.
Point b What is meant by "Emergency medical treatment for victims" is when the victim suffers sufficiently severe injuries, then village/sub-district officials or medical personnel or security officers or family/community members who are aware of the occurrence of the act of violence must bring the victim to the nearest service facility to provide emergency assistance before the victim is taken to the hospital for further treatment.
Paragraph 2 Sufficiently clear

CHAPTER V
COMPLAINT AND HANDLING PROCEDURES
Article 25
(1) Complaints of violence victims to P2TP2A may be submitted by the victim, family, community members, police officers, volunteer assistants, or social workers.
(2) The head or officers present at P2TP2A are obligated to serve victims based on the provisions as referred to in Article 21.
(3) The head or officers of P2TP2A shall immediately handle victims in accordance with established procedures.
(4) The head or officers of P2TP2A, within a maximum period of 24 (twenty-four) hours from receiving the victim's complaint, are obligated to report it to the nearest police officer.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is Central Maluku Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent together with the relevant Regional Apparatus Organizations as elements of the Regional Government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Central Maluku.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution of Central Maluku Regency as an element of the Regional Government administration.
5. Agency is the Agency that administers government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.
6. Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPT PPA is an institution established by the provincial or regency/city regional government to provide services to women and children experiencing criminal and civil problems.
7. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide prevention, protection, handling and fulfillment of the rights of women and children victims of violence by providing complaint services, medical services, social rehabilitation, legal aid, as well as social reintegration and repatriation.
8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
9. Woman is a woman who has reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years or more.
10. Violence against women (and children) is any act against a person, especially women (and children), that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually and/or economic loss.
11. Victim of violence is a woman and/or child who experiences suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or economic loss as a result of an act of violence.
12. Prevention is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women and/or children carried out by the government, family, social institutions or other community institutions, police, prosecutor's office or other parties to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and/or children.
13. 16 Days of Activism Against Violence Against Women (and Children) Campaign is a campaign to encourage efforts to eliminate violence against women (and children) throughout the world, which is held annually for 16 days from November 25 to December 10.
14. Protection of women and children is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the government, family, social institutions or other community institutions, police, prosecutor's office, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions or determinations, in connection with acts of violence against women and children.
15. Spiritual guidance service is recovery carried out with a spiritual, belief and religious approach.
16. Complaint service is a series of actions carried out by UPT PPA organizers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence.
17. Health rehabilitation service is the recovery of victims of violence from the health problems they suffer.
18. Medicolegal service is medical service and operational service in the field of medicine and law, including visum examination.
19. Social Rehabilitation Service is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
20. Legal Aid Service is legal services provided by legal aid providers free of charge to legal aid recipients.
21. Repatriation service is an effort to return victims of violence to their area of origin or to family, substitute family or community.
22. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, substitute family and community that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
23. Recovery is medical/psychiatric and psychological action toward victims of violence as an effort to restore the physical and psychological condition of victims to their original state.
24. Companion is a person trusted by the victim to accompany them during the criminal justice process.
25. Paralegal Assistance is legal assistance by a companion who does not have qualifications as a legal practitioner.
26. Health facility is a hospital, community health center, auxiliary community health center, clinic, village health post, midwife/nurse/paramedic/doctor practice place.
27. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for relevant agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of violence.
28. Safe House is temporary housing provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined operational standards.
29. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
30. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband wife and child, or father and child, or mother and child, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward or sideways up to the third degree.
31. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.

Article 18
In addition to prevention efforts as referred to in Article 17, the Regional Government conducts awareness-raising efforts for the community, families and parents through:
a. increasing the quantity and quality of education, both formal, non-formal and informal;
b. opening accessibility to obtain education, training, funding, income enhancement and social services; and
c. building community participation and concern to implement prevention of acts of violence against women and children.

OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF CENTRAL MALUKU
NUMBER 5 OF 2022
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND
CHILD VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Women and children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights, so that victims need to have their dignity protected and their right to live guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence against women and children is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for women and children physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

The existence of women and child victims of violence has not yet received adequate services, therefore comprehensive implementation of Protection for Women and Children is required.

In 2014 the Regional Government and DPRD established Regional Regulation Number 12 concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children. However, the said PERDA requires amendments related to institutional matters to be aligned with the latest regulations at the National level. In addition, the PERDA has also not comprehensively regulated matters related to protection implementation efforts that guarantee the fulfillment of victims' rights to truth, justice, recovery and guarantees of non-recurrence of cases, therefore a new regional regulation is needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This new Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for Women and Children particularly in terms of institutional matters, forms and mechanisms of prevention, prevention of acts of violence, accompaniment mechanisms, services for victims of acts of violence and empowerment of victims of acts of violence.

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is Central Maluku Regency.

4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution of Central Maluku Regency as an element of the Regional Government administration.
5. Agency is the Agency that administers government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

7. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide prevention, protection, handling and fulfillment of the rights of women and children victims of violence by providing complaint services, medical services, social rehabilitation, legal aid, as well as social reintegration and repatriation.
8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
9. Woman is a woman who has reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years or more.
10. Violence against women (and children) is any act against a person, especially women (and children), that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually and/or economic loss.
11. Victim of violence is a woman and/or child who experiences suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or economic loss as a result of an act of violence.
12. Prevention is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women and/or children carried out by the government, family, social institutions or other community institutions, police, prosecutor's office or other parties to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and/or children.
13. 16 Days of Activism Against Violence Against Women (and Children) Campaign is a campaign to encourage efforts to eliminate violence against women (and children) throughout the world, which is held annually for 16 days from November 25 to December 10.
14. Protection of women and children is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the government, family, social institutions or other community institutions, police, prosecutor's office, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions or determinations, in connection with acts of violence against women and children.
15. Spiritual guidance service is recovery carried out with a spiritual, belief and religious approach.
16. Complaint service is a series of actions carried out by UPT PPA organizers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence.
17. Health rehabilitation service is the recovery of victims of violence from the health problems they suffer.
18. Medicolegal service is medical service and operational service in the field of medicine and law, including visum examination.
19. Social Rehabilitation Service is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
20. Legal Aid Service is legal services provided by legal aid providers free of charge to legal aid recipients.
21. Repatriation service is an effort to return victims of violence to their area of origin or to family, substitute family or community.
22. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, substitute family and community that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
23. Recovery is medical/psychiatric and psychological action toward victims of violence as an effort to restore the physical and psychological condition of victims to their original state.
24. Companion is a person trusted by the victim to accompany them during the criminal justice process.
25. Paralegal Assistance is legal assistance by a companion who does not have qualifications as a legal practitioner.
26. Health facility is a hospital, community health center, auxiliary community health center, clinic, village health post, midwife/nurse/paramedic/doctor practice place.
27. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for relevant agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of violence.
28. Safe House is temporary housing provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined operational standards.
29. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
30. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband wife and child, or father and child, or mother and child, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward or sideways up to the third degree.
31. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.

OF

CONCERNING

CHILD VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Women and children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights, so that victims need to have their dignity protected and their right to live guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence against women and children is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for women and children physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

The existence of women and child victims of violence has not yet received adequate services, therefore comprehensive implementation of Protection for Women and Children is required.

In 2014 the Regional Government and DPRD established Regional Regulation Number 12 concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children. However, the said PERDA requires amendments related to institutional matters to be aligned with the latest regulations at the National level. In addition, the PERDA has also not comprehensively regulated matters related to protection implementation efforts that guarantee the fulfillment of victims' rights to truth, justice, recovery and guarantees of non-recurrence of cases, therefore a new regional regulation is needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This new Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for Women and Children particularly in terms of institutional matters, forms and mechanisms of prevention, prevention of acts of violence, accompaniment mechanisms, services for victims of acts of violence and empowerment of victims of acts of violence.

Article 10
The obligations and responsibilities of the family and/or parents as referred to in Article 7 letter c include:
a. preventing all forms of violence and protecting women and children as family members.
b. providing support for women and child victims of violence who are members of their family.

CHAPTER VII

Article 31
(1) Regional Government is obligated to conduct guidance on the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence including technical guidance and training.
(2) Regional Government is obligated to conduct supervision and evaluation of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.
(3) Supervision and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be conducted with professional, transparent, accountable principles.
(4) In addition to supervision conducted by Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (2), the community may conduct supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.
(5) Supervision conducted by the community as referred to in paragraph (4) shall be by means of conveying aspirations to the Regent or DPRD.

Article 35
(1) Regional Governments may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations, or civil society organizations that carry out protection for women and children victims of violence.
(2) Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided in accordance with the regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF CENTRAL MALUKU
NUMBER 5 OF 2022
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND
CHILD VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Women and children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights, so that victims need to have their dignity protected and their right to live guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence against women and children is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for women and children physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

The existence of women and child victims of violence has not yet received adequate services, therefore comprehensive implementation of Protection for Women and Children is required.

In 2014 the Regional Government and DPRD established Regional Regulation Number 12 concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children. However, the said PERDA requires amendments related to institutional matters to be aligned with the latest regulations at the National level. In addition, the PERDA has also not comprehensively regulated matters related to protection implementation efforts that guarantee the fulfillment of victims' rights to truth, justice, recovery and guarantees of non-recurrence of cases, therefore a new regional regulation is needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This new Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for Women and Children particularly in terms of institutional matters, forms and mechanisms of prevention, prevention of acts of violence, accompaniment mechanisms, services for victims of acts of violence and empowerment of victims of acts of violence.

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Women and children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights, so that victims need to have their dignity protected and their right to live guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence against women and children is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for women and children physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

The existence of women and child victims of violence has not yet received adequate services, therefore comprehensive implementation of Protection for Women and Children is required.

In 2014 the Regional Government and DPRD established Regional Regulation Number 12 concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children. However, the said PERDA requires amendments related to institutional matters to be aligned with the latest regulations at the National level. In addition, the PERDA has also not comprehensively regulated matters related to protection implementation efforts that guarantee the fulfillment of victims' rights to truth, justice, recovery and guarantees of non-recurrence of cases, therefore a new regional regulation is needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This new Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for Women and Children particularly in terms of institutional matters, forms and mechanisms of prevention, prevention of acts of violence, accompaniment mechanisms, services for victims of acts of violence and empowerment of victims of acts of violence.

Article 27
(1) In handling victims, P2TP2A is obligated to establish networks with government or private hospitals for treatment and health recovery.
(2) In the event it is necessary, P2TP2A may also establish networks with social protection houses or trauma centers owned by the government or community, or safe houses owned by the government or community, or other social service institutions.

CHAPTER X
FINANCING
Article 34
(1) The Regional Government is obligated to provide expenditure budget every year through the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget as well as other legitimate and non-binding sources of income to finance the implementation of prevention, protection and recovery tasks for women and children victims of violence.
(2) The budget for prevention, protection and recovery activities for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is attached to the relevant Agency and managed by P2TP2A in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

CHAPTER V
COMPLAINT AND HANDLING PROCEDURES
Article 25
(1) Complaints of violence victims to P2TP2A may be submitted by the victim, family, community members, police officers, volunteer assistants, or social workers.
(2) The head or officers present at P2TP2A are obligated to serve victims based on the provisions as referred to in Article 21.
(3) The head or officers of P2TP2A shall immediately handle victims in accordance with established procedures.
(4) The head or officers of P2TP2A, within a maximum period of 24 (twenty-four) hours from receiving the victim's complaint, are obligated to report it to the nearest police officer.

Article 13
(1) The objectives of establishing P2TP2A are:
a. to facilitate the needs of women and children victims of violence in fulfilling the rights of victims, namely the right to truth, justice, recovery and guarantee of non-recurrence of cases; and
b. to realize welfare, justice and Gender equality in various fields of life for women and children comprehensively.
(2) The main duties of P2TP2A are:
a. to carry out efforts to prevent violence against women and children;
b. to carry out handling efforts for women and children victims of violence; and
c. to carry out rehabilitation efforts including recovery, empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence.
(3) The functions of P2TP2A are:
a. as a data and information center regarding women and children;
b. as a service center for women and children victims of violence; and
c. as an empowerment center for women and children.

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Women and children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights, so that victims need to have their dignity protected and their right to live guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence against women and children is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for women and children physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

The existence of women and child victims of violence has not yet received adequate services, therefore comprehensive implementation of Protection for Women and Children is required.

In 2014 the Regional Government and DPRD established Regional Regulation Number 12 concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children. However, the said PERDA requires amendments related to institutional matters to be aligned with the latest regulations at the National level. In addition, the PERDA has also not comprehensively regulated matters related to protection implementation efforts that guarantee the fulfillment of victims' rights to truth, justice, recovery and guarantees of non-recurrence of cases, therefore a new regional regulation is needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This new Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for Women and Children particularly in terms of institutional matters, forms and mechanisms of prevention, prevention of acts of violence, accompaniment mechanisms, services for victims of acts of violence and empowerment of victims of acts of violence.

(2) Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided in accordance with the regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is Central Maluku Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent together with the relevant Regional Apparatus Organizations as elements of the Regional Government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Central Maluku.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution of Central Maluku Regency as an element of the Regional Government administration.
5. Agency is the Agency that administers government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.
6. Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPT PPA is an institution established by the provincial or regency/city regional government to provide services to women and children experiencing criminal and civil problems.
7. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide prevention, protection, handling and fulfillment of the rights of women and children victims of violence by providing complaint services, medical services, social rehabilitation, legal aid, as well as social reintegration and repatriation.
8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
9. Woman is a woman who has reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years or more.
10. Violence against women (and children) is any act against a person, especially women (and children), that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually and/or economic loss.
11. Victim of violence is a woman and/or child who experiences suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or economic loss as a result of an act of violence.
12. Prevention is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women and/or children carried out by the government, family, social institutions or other community institutions, police, prosecutor's office or other parties to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and/or children.
13. 16 Days of Activism Against Violence Against Women (and Children) Campaign is a campaign to encourage efforts to eliminate violence against women (and children) throughout the world, which is held annually for 16 days from November 25 to December 10.
14. Protection of women and children is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the government, family, social institutions or other community institutions, police, prosecutor's office, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions or determinations, in connection with acts of violence against women and children.
15. Spiritual guidance service is recovery carried out with a spiritual, belief and religious approach.
16. Complaint service is a series of actions carried out by UPT PPA organizers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence.
17. Health rehabilitation service is the recovery of victims of violence from the health problems they suffer.
18. Medicolegal service is medical service and operational service in the field of medicine and law, including visum examination.
19. Social Rehabilitation Service is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
20. Legal Aid Service is legal services provided by legal aid providers free of charge to legal aid recipients.
21. Repatriation service is an effort to return victims of violence to their area of origin or to family, substitute family or community.
22. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, substitute family and community that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
23. Recovery is medical/psychiatric and psychological action toward victims of violence as an effort to restore the physical and psychological condition of victims to their original state.
24. Companion is a person trusted by the victim to accompany them during the criminal justice process.
25. Paralegal Assistance is legal assistance by a companion who does not have qualifications as a legal practitioner.
26. Health facility is a hospital, community health center, auxiliary community health center, clinic, village health post, midwife/nurse/paramedic/doctor practice place.
27. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for relevant agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of violence.
28. Safe House is temporary housing provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined operational standards.
29. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
30. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband wife and child, or father and child, or mother and child, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward or sideways up to the third degree.
31. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.

CHAPTER IV
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION
Part One
Institutional

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF CENTRAL MALUKU
NUMBER 5 OF 2022
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND
CHILD VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Women and children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights, so that victims need to have their dignity protected and their right to live guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence against women and children is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for women and children physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

The existence of women and child victims of violence has not yet received adequate services, therefore comprehensive implementation of Protection for Women and Children is required.

In 2014 the Regional Government and DPRD established Regional Regulation Number 12 concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children. However, the said PERDA requires amendments related to institutional matters to be aligned with the latest regulations at the National level. In addition, the PERDA has also not comprehensively regulated matters related to protection implementation efforts that guarantee the fulfillment of victims' rights to truth, justice, recovery and guarantees of non-recurrence of cases, therefore a new regional regulation is needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This new Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for Women and Children particularly in terms of institutional matters, forms and mechanisms of prevention, prevention of acts of violence, accompaniment mechanisms, services for victims of acts of violence and empowerment of victims of acts of violence.

Article 6
In the event of an act of violence, every victim has the right to receive assistance both psychologically and legally as well as to obtain guarantees for their rights related to their status as a wife, mother, child, family member or as a member of society.

Article 10
The obligations and responsibilities of the family and/or parents as referred to in Article 7 letter c include:
a. preventing all forms of violence and protecting women and children as family members.
b. providing support for women and child victims of violence who are members of their family.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF CENTRAL MALUKU
NUMBER 5 OF 2022
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND
CHILD VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Women and children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights, so that victims need to have their dignity protected and their right to live guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence against women and children is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for women and children physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

The existence of women and child victims of violence has not yet received adequate services, therefore comprehensive implementation of Protection for Women and Children is required.

In 2014 the Regional Government and DPRD established Regional Regulation Number 12 concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children. However, the said PERDA requires amendments related to institutional matters to be aligned with the latest regulations at the National level. In addition, the PERDA has also not comprehensively regulated matters related to protection implementation efforts that guarantee the fulfillment of victims' rights to truth, justice, recovery and guarantees of non-recurrence of cases, therefore a new regional regulation is needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This new Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for Women and Children particularly in terms of institutional matters, forms and mechanisms of prevention, prevention of acts of violence, accompaniment mechanisms, services for victims of acts of violence and empowerment of victims of acts of violence.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is Central Maluku Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent together with the relevant Regional Apparatus Organizations as elements of the Regional Government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Central Maluku.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution of Central Maluku Regency as an element of the Regional Government administration.
5. Agency is the Agency that administers government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.
6. Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPT PPA is an institution established by the provincial or regency/city regional government to provide services to women and children experiencing criminal and civil problems.
7. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide prevention, protection, handling and fulfillment of the rights of women and children victims of violence by providing complaint services, medical services, social rehabilitation, legal aid, as well as social reintegration and repatriation.
8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
9. Woman is a woman who has reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years or more.
10. Violence against women (and children) is any act against a person, especially women (and children), that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually and/or economic loss.
11. Victim of violence is a woman and/or child who experiences suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or economic loss as a result of an act of violence.
12. Prevention is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women and/or children carried out by the government, family, social institutions or other community institutions, police, prosecutor's office or other parties to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and/or children.
13. 16 Days of Activism Against Violence Against Women (and Children) Campaign is a campaign to encourage efforts to eliminate violence against women (and children) throughout the world, which is held annually for 16 days from November 25 to December 10.
14. Protection of women and children is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the government, family, social institutions or other community institutions, police, prosecutor's office, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions or determinations, in connection with acts of violence against women and children.
15. Spiritual guidance service is recovery carried out with a spiritual, belief and religious approach.
16. Complaint service is a series of actions carried out by UPT PPA organizers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence.
17. Health rehabilitation service is the recovery of victims of violence from the health problems they suffer.
18. Medicolegal service is medical service and operational service in the field of medicine and law, including visum examination.
19. Social Rehabilitation Service is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
20. Legal Aid Service is legal services provided by legal aid providers free of charge to legal aid recipients.
21. Repatriation service is an effort to return victims of violence to their area of origin or to family, substitute family or community.
22. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, substitute family and community that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
23. Recovery is medical/psychiatric and psychological action toward victims of violence as an effort to restore the physical and psychological condition of victims to their original state.
24. Companion is a person trusted by the victim to accompany them during the criminal justice process.
25. Paralegal Assistance is legal assistance by a companion who does not have qualifications as a legal practitioner.
26. Health facility is a hospital, community health center, auxiliary community health center, clinic, village health post, midwife/nurse/paramedic/doctor practice place.
27. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for relevant agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of violence.
28. Safe House is temporary housing provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined operational standards.
29. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
30. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband wife and child, or father and child, or mother and child, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward or sideways up to the third degree.
31. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is Central Maluku Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent together with the relevant Regional Apparatus Organizations as elements of the Regional Government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Central Maluku.

7. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide prevention, protection, handling and fulfillment of the rights of women and children victims of violence by providing complaint services, medical services, social rehabilitation, legal aid, as well as social reintegration and repatriation.
8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
9. Woman is a woman who has reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years or more.
10. Violence against women (and children) is any act against a person, especially women (and children), that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually and/or economic loss.
11. Victim of violence is a woman and/or child who experiences suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or economic loss as a result of an act of violence.
12. Prevention is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women and/or children carried out by the government, family, social institutions or other community institutions, police, prosecutor's office or other parties to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and/or children.
13. 16 Days of Activism Against Violence Against Women (and Children) Campaign is a campaign to encourage efforts to eliminate violence against women (and children) throughout the world, which is held annually for 16 days from November 25 to December 10.
14. Protection of women and children is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the government, family, social institutions or other community institutions, police, prosecutor's office, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions or determinations, in connection with acts of violence against women and children.
15. Spiritual guidance service is recovery carried out with a spiritual, belief and religious approach.
16. Complaint service is a series of actions carried out by UPT PPA organizers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence.
17. Health rehabilitation service is the recovery of victims of violence from the health problems they suffer.
18. Medicolegal service is medical service and operational service in the field of medicine and law, including visum examination.
19. Social Rehabilitation Service is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
20. Legal Aid Service is legal services provided by legal aid providers free of charge to legal aid recipients.
21. Repatriation service is an effort to return victims of violence to their area of origin or to family, substitute family or community.
22. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, substitute family and community that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
23. Recovery is medical/psychiatric and psychological action toward victims of violence as an effort to restore the physical and psychological condition of victims to their original state.
24. Companion is a person trusted by the victim to accompany them during the criminal justice process.
25. Paralegal Assistance is legal assistance by a companion who does not have qualifications as a legal practitioner.
26. Health facility is a hospital, community health center, auxiliary community health center, clinic, village health post, midwife/nurse/paramedic/doctor practice place.
27. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for relevant agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of violence.
28. Safe House is temporary housing provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined operational standards.
29. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
30. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband wife and child, or father and child, or mother and child, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward or sideways up to the third degree.
31. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.

CHAPTER VIII

Article 32
(1) The community participates in the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of:

b. independently conducting socialization of the rights of women and children;
c. preventing the occurrence of violence;
d. providing first aid to victims; and
e. reporting to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector and mass media.

Article 30
(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector in the implementation of protection for women and children.
(2) The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1), is carried out through:

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF CENTRAL MALUKU
NUMBER 5 OF 2022
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND
CHILD VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Women and children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights, so that victims need to have their dignity protected and their right to live guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence against women and children is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for women and children physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

The existence of women and child victims of violence has not yet received adequate services, therefore comprehensive implementation of Protection for Women and Children is required.

In 2014 the Regional Government and DPRD established Regional Regulation Number 12 concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children. However, the said PERDA requires amendments related to institutional matters to be aligned with the latest regulations at the National level. In addition, the PERDA has also not comprehensively regulated matters related to protection implementation efforts that guarantee the fulfillment of victims' rights to truth, justice, recovery and guarantees of non-recurrence of cases, therefore a new regional regulation is needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This new Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for Women and Children particularly in terms of institutional matters, forms and mechanisms of prevention, prevention of acts of violence, accompaniment mechanisms, services for victims of acts of violence and empowerment of victims of acts of violence.

Article 21
(1) In addition to the forms of services as referred to in Article 20, the Regional Government through P2TP2A is obligated to provide temporary protection services for victims including, but not limited to:
 a. initial rescue of victims from acts of violence; and
 b. emergency medical treatment for victims.
(2) To provide protection as referred to in paragraph (1), P2TP2A may cooperate with security forces, the Negeri Government and Administrative Negeri, kelurahan, customary leaders and/or groups in the community that provide assistance services for women and children victims of violence

CHAPTER VII
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 31
(1) Regional Government is obligated to conduct guidance on the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence including technical guidance and training.
(2) Regional Government is obligated to conduct supervision and evaluation of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.
(3) Supervision and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be conducted with professional, transparent, accountable principles.
(4) In addition to supervision conducted by Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (2), the community may conduct supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.
(5) Supervision conducted by the community as referred to in paragraph (4) shall be by means of conveying aspirations to the Regent or DPRD.

Article 35
(1) Regional Governments may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations, or civil society organizations that carry out protection for women and children victims of violence.
(2) Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided in accordance with the regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 31
(1) Regional Government is obligated to conduct guidance on the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence including technical guidance and training.

CHILD VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Women and children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights, so that victims need to have their dignity protected and their right to live guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence against women and children is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for women and children physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

The existence of women and child victims of violence has not yet received adequate services, therefore comprehensive implementation of Protection for Women and Children is required.

In 2014 the Regional Government and DPRD established Regional Regulation Number 12 concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children. However, the said PERDA requires amendments related to institutional matters to be aligned with the latest regulations at the National level. In addition, the PERDA has also not comprehensively regulated matters related to protection implementation efforts that guarantee the fulfillment of victims' rights to truth, justice, recovery and guarantees of non-recurrence of cases, therefore a new regional regulation is needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This new Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for Women and Children particularly in terms of institutional matters, forms and mechanisms of prevention, prevention of acts of violence, accompaniment mechanisms, services for victims of acts of violence and empowerment of victims of acts of violence.

PREVENTION, PROTECTION AND RECOVERY
Article 7

b. community, social organizations and/or other community organizations in accordance with applicable laws and regulations; and

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is Central Maluku Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent together with the relevant Regional Apparatus Organizations as elements of the Regional Government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Central Maluku.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution of Central Maluku Regency as an element of the Regional Government administration.
5. Agency is the Agency that administers government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.
6. Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPT PPA is an institution established by the provincial or regency/city regional government to provide services to women and children experiencing criminal and civil problems.
7. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide prevention, protection, handling and fulfillment of the rights of women and children victims of violence by providing complaint services, medical services, social rehabilitation, legal aid, as well as social reintegration and repatriation.
8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
9. Woman is a woman who has reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years or more.
10. Violence against women (and children) is any act against a person, especially women (and children), that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually and/or economic loss.
11. Victim of violence is a woman and/or child who experiences suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or economic loss as a result of an act of violence.
12. Prevention is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women and/or children carried out by the government, family, social institutions or other community institutions, police, prosecutor's office or other parties to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and/or children.
13. 16 Days of Activism Against Violence Against Women (and Children) Campaign is a campaign to encourage efforts to eliminate violence against women (and children) throughout the world, which is held annually for 16 days from November 25 to December 10.
14. Protection of women and children is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the government, family, social institutions or other community institutions, police, prosecutor's office, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions or determinations, in connection with acts of violence against women and children.
15. Spiritual guidance service is recovery carried out with a spiritual, belief and religious approach.
16. Complaint service is a series of actions carried out by UPT PPA organizers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence.
17. Health rehabilitation service is the recovery of victims of violence from the health problems they suffer.
18. Medicolegal service is medical service and operational service in the field of medicine and law, including visum examination.
19. Social Rehabilitation Service is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
20. Legal Aid Service is legal services provided by legal aid providers free of charge to legal aid recipients.
21. Repatriation service is an effort to return victims of violence to their area of origin or to family, substitute family or community.
22. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, substitute family and community that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
23. Recovery is medical/psychiatric and psychological action toward victims of violence as an effort to restore the physical and psychological condition of victims to their original state.
24. Companion is a person trusted by the victim to accompany them during the criminal justice process.
25. Paralegal Assistance is legal assistance by a companion who does not have qualifications as a legal practitioner.
26. Health facility is a hospital, community health center, auxiliary community health center, clinic, village health post, midwife/nurse/paramedic/doctor practice place.
27. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for relevant agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of violence.
28. Safe House is temporary housing provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined operational standards.
29. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
30. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband wife and child, or father and child, or mother and child, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward or sideways up to the third degree.
31. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.

OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF CENTRAL MALUKU
NUMBER 5 OF 2022
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND
CHILD VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Women and children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights, so that victims need to have their dignity protected and their right to live guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence against women and children is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for women and children physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

The existence of women and child victims of violence has not yet received adequate services, therefore comprehensive implementation of Protection for Women and Children is required.

In 2014 the Regional Government and DPRD established Regional Regulation Number 12 concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children. However, the said PERDA requires amendments related to institutional matters to be aligned with the latest regulations at the National level. In addition, the PERDA has also not comprehensively regulated matters related to protection implementation efforts that guarantee the fulfillment of victims' rights to truth, justice, recovery and guarantees of non-recurrence of cases, therefore a new regional regulation is needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This new Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for Women and Children particularly in terms of institutional matters, forms and mechanisms of prevention, prevention of acts of violence, accompaniment mechanisms, services for victims of acts of violence and empowerment of victims of acts of violence.
